perspective:
Harold Padilla’s accessible information:

- He is a project manager dealing with a project whose progress is suffering because his team seems unmotivated/underperforming.
- He feels frustrated, anxious, and at his wit’s end about this.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a police officer friend/advice source. He arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur.
- He heard Arthur say motivation can be tricky and that Harold should understand what drives each team member individually. Arthur advised one-on-one conversations so people feel valued and understood.
- Harold admitted he had been focusing on project goals/deadlines rather than personal motivations. He said he would try Arthur’s advice and felt more hopeful.
- Harold told his team he wanted one-on-one chats to understand their motivations. He heard Team Member 1 and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each and work toward project success.
- Later, Harold observed the team still not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried.
- He told Arthur he had tried the suggestions but the team still wasn’t responding. He heard Arthur suggest deeper issues might be at play: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper.
- Harold said he would set up another round of meetings.
- Harold then held one-on-one meetings to investigate team dynamics. He asked team members to share concerns.
- He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension among a few team members affecting work. Harold said he would look into resolving conflicts.
- He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold said he would see if tasks could be redistributed and that their well-being mattered.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered. He told the team he would implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive, open environment.
- He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and would help them work better together. He heard Team Member 2 agree that it was good concerns were being addressed.
- Harold said their input and well-being were crucial to the project’s success.

Harold does not have access to hidden events, other characters’ private thoughts, or narrator-only information beyond what he observed, heard, said, did, or felt.
